maria: Quick check — weights are uploaded to s3://redwood-models/opt-12b/v2/ (manifest.json included). Spinning up a staging bundle for serving-readiness tests. Can someone validate config knobs before I open the PR?
chen: I see the manifest, path looks fine. double-check that weights are in shards: s3://redwood-models/opt-12b/v2/shard-000[0-3].bin. Also confirm model_family in model config is "opt" so kernel selection picks the fused attention.
sam: Heads up — tokenizer has a subtle difference: eos token is missing in the provided tokenizer.json. If you don't set eos_token explicitly we get `tokenizer.eos_token_id == None` and prompt-truncation breaks. Quick fix in the serving config:
```
model_config:
  tokenizer:
    override_tokens:
      eos_token: "</s>"
```
This matches how we onboarded opt-6b.
ewan: Continuous-batching knobs I used in perf runs:
- max_batch_tokens: 8192
- batch_timeout_ms: 15
- max_concurrent_batches: 4
We saw tail latency under 100ms in staging with these.

[2026-03-15T14:02:01Z] RuntimeError: tokenizer.eos_token_id is None

maria: thanks — Sam can you push a tiny patch to the model config to inject eos override? I'll re-run validator.
sam: pushed -> PR #4125. includes override and also sets `prefix_cache_ttl_s: 120` as a conservative default for this prefix-heavy workload.
chen: scheduler note — recommend `routing.policy: latency_priority` for the initial rollout (small fraction) then A/B to `cost_priority` for larger traffic. Also add `fallback_model: opt-12b-quant` in case of capacity.
